input: Audit all my streaming subscriptions this week

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Streaming could mean video only (Netflix, Hulu) or also music, podcasts, audiobooks, gaming, and software — the breadth changes the whole inventory list.
If the audit covers a household with multiple members, shared or family plans need to be evaluated differently than personal subscriptions.
Knowing where subscriptions are billed (credit cards, PayPal, Apple/Google store) determines where to look to find them all.
Whether there is a target monthly spend or a hard budget ceiling directly shapes the decision criteria for keeping vs. cutting services.
Done well could mean simply listing everything, or it could mean actively cancelling underused services — the end goal defines how far the audit goes.
The decision framework matters — some people prioritise cost savings above all, others weigh usage frequency, content quality, or whether services are bundled.
A preferred format for tracking (spreadsheet, notes app, pen and paper) determines what deliverable to build and what the immediate first action is.

gold.taskTitle: Audit all my streaming subscriptions this week
gold.taskDescription: Review all current streaming service subscriptions to assess usage, cost, and whether to keep, cancel, or change each one.

questions.title: Which types of streaming services are included in this audit?
questions.description: Does the audit cover only video streaming (e.g. Netflix, Disney+), or also music, podcasts, audiobooks, cloud gaming, and software subscriptions?

questions.title: Is this audit just for you or your whole household?
questions.description: Clarifies whether shared or family-plan subscriptions used by a partner, children, or roommates need to be included and evaluated together.

questions.title: Where are your subscriptions currently being billed?
questions.description: Identifies which payment methods or storefronts (credit card, PayPal, Apple ID, Google Play) to check so no subscriptions are missed.

questions.title: Do you have a target monthly spend you want to reach?
questions.description: A specific budget ceiling or savings goal gives a concrete benchmark for deciding which services to keep versus cancel.

questions.title: What does a successful audit look like when you are done?
questions.description: Determines whether the finish line is a complete inventory list, a set of cancellation decisions, or confirmed changes already actioned on all accounts.

questions.title: What matters most when deciding to keep a service?
questions.description: Surfaces the user's priority — for example, cost per month, how often they actually watch or listen, content exclusives, or bundle value.

questions.title: What format do you want to track everything in?
questions.description: Establishes the tool or deliverable — such as a spreadsheet, a notes app, or a simple list — so the first concrete action is clear.
